title: Range-read iterator fallback notes (personal)
content:
Context / symptom:
- Intermittent failures when loading a 4-shard checkpoint from GCS during cold start of dedicated pool (shard sizes ~12GB). App reports: "Unexpected EOF while filling buffer" and model loader falls back to full-download path then times out. Failure rate ~2-3% on first load after node boot; subsequent retries sometimes succeed.

Observed error snippets (collected from logs):
- "ERROR ckpt.loader: ReadError: got 0 bytes from range request (expected 1048576)"
- "Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/ckpt/reader.py\", line 182, in _range_iter
    chunk = resp.raw.read(n)
  File \"/usr/lib/python3.11/http/client.py\", line 477, in read
    return self._read_next_chunked_block()
  File \"/usr/lib/python3.11/http/client.py\", line 649, in _read_next_chunked_block
    raise IncompleteRead(bytes_read, size)
IncompleteRead: 0 bytes read, 1048576 expected"
- "grpc: downstream stream reset by peer during copy_to_kv" (observed when streaming into KV cache)

Things I tried (commands + small tests):
1) Repro with curl range requests vs python requests-
- curl -v -H "Range: bytes=0-1048575" "https://storage.googleapis.com/bucket/checkpoints/shard-0000"  - sometimes returned full 1MB chunk, sometimes returned fewer bytes but with 200 OK (not 206)
- python snippet used requests.get(range header, stream=True) and iterated resp.raw.read(1MB). Repro of IncompleteRead occurred after ~30-50 iterations in a tight loop on same VM under load.

2) Disabled HTTP/2 proxy (env var to force HTTP/1.1 to GCS)-
- Set GRPC_HTTP2=0 on worker and retested; failure rate went down but didn't go to zero.

3) Bumped socket timeouts and retried at higher level-
- Loader now does up to 3 range-retries per chunk with exponential backoff (100ms -> 300ms -> 900ms). Reduced failures by ~50% in isolated runs.

4) Forced single-threaded range iteration (no parallel chunk pulls)-
- Under load this increased latency but made results more stable; suggests a resource/connection exhaustion race.

5) Reproduced with gsutil cp (full download), which never fails in these repro runs, so full-download path is stable; range reads are the fragility point.

Hypotheses:
A) Proxying / HTTP/2 multiplexing between node and GCS causes head / connection resets for large parallel range reads; some clients receive a truncated response (0-length) instead of an error.
B) Server-side transient: GCS occasionally responds with 200 OK and shorter-than-requested body when Range header is malformed or connection cut; our code treats non-206 as OK and tries to read exact bytes, triggering IncompleteRead. Need to be strict about status code.
C) Local connection resource exhaustion: when many range requests are in-flight, the http client library may reuse/close sockets unexpectedly under heavy GC or when ephemeral file descriptors reach limit.
D) Interaction with our KV streaming: gRPC downstream reset happens when we try to push partial bytes into the KV stream while another coroutine cancels; cancellation leaves upstream read hanging and next attempt misreads state.

Quick wins to validate hypotheses:
- Add explicit check: require resp.status_code == 206 for range requests. If not 206, abort and retry (instead of trying to read N bytes).
- Add a defensive loop around resp.raw.read to handle short reads and re-issue a range request for remaining bytes instead of raising immediately.
- Instrument per-connection FD counts and active HTTP connections (netstat) in repro runs.
- Run with HTTP/1.1 pinned and compare metrics vs default HTTP/2.

Instrumentation findings so far:
- Many of the failing requests show resp.status_code == 200 (not 206). The server sent whole-object with content-length ~shard size but connection closed early: chunked behavior seems inconsistent.
- FD usage spikes correlated with number of parallel chunk fetchers * 2 (we open a few internal file handles and HTTP streams per chunk). Some test VMs hit ulimit 1024 in extreme runs.
- When running with trunked parallelism 8 -> 32 chunkers, failures increase roughly linearly.

Notes on code points of interest:
- ckpt/reader.py::_range_iter (generator yields contiguous chunk bytes) -- current impl assumes resp.raw.read(n) returns exactly n or raises. Need to handle partial reads and EAGAIN-like behavior.
- transport/http_client_wrapper.py -- wraps requests.Session to set headers + retry. Might be swallowing 206 vs 200 differences.
- kv/stream_writer.py::copy_to_kv -- expects deterministic chunk sizes; if input is shorter, triggers grpc reset path which cancels upstream and can cascade.

Immediate patch idea (small, low-risk):
1) In _range_iter: assert resp.status_code == 206; if status != 206, log response headers and body prefix, then raise a RetryableRead to let upper layer requeue shard fetch.
2) Implement read_exact(fd, n) that loops until n bytes read or until explicit connection-close. If short read, compute remaining byte-range and re-issue a Range request starting at that offset (idempotent).
3) Add a per-shard semaphore to cap concurrency (start with 8) to limit FD and socket pressure.

Longer-term changes to consider:
- Switch to resumable multipart download API (compose/objects with rewriteToken) for very large shards to avoid many small range reads.
- Consider switching weight storage layout to smaller chunk objects (e.g., 8MB objects) so range reads are fewer and easier to retry. Tradeoff: more objects -> list cost and eventual consistency considerations.
- Add end-to-end test harness that spins up a small HTTP server that intentionally returns 200 but truncated bodies to validate our retry logic.

Repro notes + minimal script used locally:
- Small python repro (attached below) used to hit GCS with range headers and loop: it reproduces IncompleteRead in ~1-2 minutes on busy vm with parallelism 24.
- Example curl load: for i in $(seq 0 23); do RANGE_START=$((i*1048576)); curl -s -H "Range: bytes=${RANGE_START}-${RANGE_START}+1048575" https://storage.googleapis.com/bucket/checkpoints/shard-0001 & done

Next steps (for me):
- Add quick assert on status_code == 206 and re-run smoke tests across dedicated pools (today).
- Add read_exact fallback and per-shard semaphore by EOD; push to canary for 24h.
- Loop Leo in for FD/uLimits check and Kai to review KV cancellation semantics.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there a documented GCS behavior that returns 200 for range requests in some circumstances? (ask infra / GCS docs)
- Do our HTTP client libraries collapse chunked responses into raw reads that could return fewer bytes when connection is reused?
- Should we consider exponential backoff with jitter at range-chunk level to avoid synchronized retry storms?

Random notes / ideas recorded while investigating:
- Could use a 1MB chunk cache with LRU keyed by (object, offset) to reduce repeated range reads across retries.
- If we switch to smaller objects, store a compact manifest with chunk offsets/version to avoid long list calls during load.

If anyone wants to reproduce quickly, ping me and I'll share the small repro script + VM image that exhibits the behavior.

-- Isabel
